title: Finite smooth trace and coefficient reduction over an arbitrary ground field
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $k$ be any field of characteristic different from $\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], smooth of pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $n\geq1$ set $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and for $T=X,Y$ write $A_{n,T}$ for its constant sheaf on $T$. On each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$ consist of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology in the intrinsic finite-stratification sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude: there are integers $a\leq b$ such that tensoring with any sheaf of $A_n$-modules in degree zero has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let $Rf_{!,n}$ be compact-support direct image, formed by proper direct image after extension by zero in a compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and define its constructible exceptional inverse image as follows. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison and $f_n^\times$ for the right adjoint of ordinary etale compact-support direct image. For $K$ of bounded constructible etale origin $K_0$, put $Rf_n^!K=\nu_X^*f_n^\times K_0$, using the fully faithful comparison to identify different choices of $K_0$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Preservation of bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude for this smooth $f$ is part of the assertion below. Write $A_{n,T}(1)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}$, the sheaf of $\ell^n$-th roots of unity, $A_{n,T}(d)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}^{\otimes_{A_n}d}$ with zeroth power $A_{n,T}$, and $K(d)=K\otimes^L_{A_n} A_{n,T}(d)$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf].

For each $A=A_n$, use ordinary etale coefficients to form $\omega_{f,A}=f_A^\times A_Y$. Let $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. Its normal bundle is $T_{X/Y}$, with projection $\pi:T_{X/Y}\to X$ and zero section $z$ [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. Define the orientation $\alpha_{f,A}:\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$ by the composite
$$\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta^*\omega_{p_1,A}\xrightarrow{\delta_{p_1,\Delta}}z^*\omega_{\pi,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d].$$
The first arrow is diagonal pullback of the exceptional base-change map [prop-asd-smooth-base-change], the second is the normalized deformation comparison [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization], and the last is the pullback of the inverse of the vector-bundle purity map adjoint to Kummer-normalized integration [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity]. Let $\phi_{f,A,K_0}:f^*K_0\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\to f_A^\times K_0$ be the canonical tensor map, the transpose of the compact-support projection formula followed by $1\otimes\varepsilon_{A_Y}$ [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. Define $\gamma_{n,K}$ to be the etale/pro-etale transport of
$$f^*K_0(d)[2d]\cong f^*K_0\otimes_A^LA_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{1\otimes\alpha_{f,A}^{-1}}f^*K_0\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\phi_{f,A,K_0}}f_A^\times K_0.$$
Then $\gamma_{n,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!K$ is a natural isomorphism in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. Its adjoint trace is the counit composed with $Rf_{!,n}(\gamma_{n,K})$; this specifies its normalization by the Kummer/projective-line integration and the diagonal/deformation construction. At $d=0$ it is the etale adjunction.

For every $r\geq m\geq1$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_r)$, let $S_T=(-)\otimes_{A_r}^LA_m$. Let $b_M:S_YRf_{!,r}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,m}S_XM$ be the canonical compactification coefficient map. The exceptional coefficient comparison $c_K:S_XRf_r^!K\to Rf_m^!S_YK$ is the transpose determined by
$$\varepsilon_m(S_YK)\circ Rf_{!,m}(c_K)=S_Y(\varepsilon_r(K))\circ b_{Rf_r^!K}^{-1}.$$
It is an isomorphism, and, under the canonical pullback and twist identification $\lambda_K:S_X(Lf^*K(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*S_YK(d)[2d]$, one has
$$c_K\circ S_X(\gamma_{r,K})=\gamma_{m,S_YK}\circ\lambda_K.$$
For $r\geq m\geq n\geq1$, these compact-support, exceptional, pullback, twist, and purity comparisons for $A_r\to A_n$ agree with the successive comparisons through $A_m$ under tensor associativity (the quotient cocycle). For $K=A_{n,Y}$ the source and target of $\gamma_{n,K}$ have constructible cohomology only in degree $-2d$, and their reductions satisfy this same cocycle.

source.place: sk-thm-smooth-purity and proof: inverse diagonal orientation followed by the tensor map; sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md: diagonal, deformation, vector bundle; sk-lem-sp-reduction.proof.md and sk-lem-sp-reduction-compatibilities.proof.md: counit-defined coefficient comparisons and quotient cocycle. The ordinary-etale Noetherian formulation retains arbitrary ground fields.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and itself; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] therefore makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. The graph of $f$ is a closed immersion into $X\times_kY$ because $Y$ is separated over $k$. The projection $X\times_kY\to Y$ is the base change of the finite-type structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so the graph-to-$Y$ composite (which is $f$) is separated and finite type. By [thm-nagata-compactification] it has a compactification $f=qj$ over the qcqs Noetherian base $Y$. The same applies to the smooth maps, vector bundles and deformation spaces used below: they are separated finite type over Noetherian schemes. For each $A=A_n$, [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies $P_A=Rf^{\mathrm{et}}_{!,A}\dashv G_A=f_A^\times$. The canonical comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] identify compactification choices on the bounded-below objects used here. All later constructions are on these ordinary etale categories until the final transport; no ambient unbounded pro-etale right adjoint is asserted.

source.place: Finite-existence input, with ordinary Noetherian compactification and adjoint prerequisites

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], every intrinsic bounded constructible pro-etale $K$ has etale origin $K_0$. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$. This functor is exact [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], fully faithful on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and preserves derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. If $K$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, then for each ordinary etale module sheaf $M$, $C_Y(K_0\otimes_A^LM)=K\otimes_A^LC_YM$ vanishes outside that interval. Exactness and full faithfulness on degree-zero sheaves detect zero cohomology, so $K_0$ has the same Tor interval. Take its bounded flat representative $Q$ in $[a,b]$ by [lem-sf-etale-flat-model]; it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For any quotient $A=A_r\to B=A_m$, $Q\otimes_AB$ is flat over $B$: tensoring it with a short exact sequence of $B$-module sheaves is tensoring $Q$ with the same exact sequence of underlying $A$-module sheaves. Its interval remains $[a,b]$, and derived associativity identifies $((Q\otimes_AB)\otimes_BC)$ with $Q\otimes_AC$ by $(q\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto q\otimes bc$. Derived tensor is defined even for non-flat quotients by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Apply [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] on the pro-etale site to $C_YK_0$ and the finite constant second factor $B$, with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Tensor preservation identifies the resulting tensor with $C_Y(K_0\otimes_A^LB)$. The origin equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] reflects constructibility of its cohomology sheaves back to the ordinary etale site; the bounded model already gives its finite cohomological interval. Thus the cited pro-etale tensor lemma is not being applied directly on the ordinary etale site. A constructible $A$-module sheaf annihilated by the kernel of $A\to B$ is constructible as a $B$-module sheaf: on a trivializing cover its $A$-linear transition maps are $B$-linear, and its finite stalks are finite over $B$. Consequently reduction stays in the stated intrinsic categories, and has bounded constructible etale origin again.

source.place: Coefficient extension on bounded flat models; intrinsic finite-Tor and constructibility checks

proof.text: Construct $b_M:S_YP_AM\to P_BS_XM$, where $S=(-)\otimes_A^LB$, on one compactification $f=qj$. The open tensor map $S(j_!Q)\to j_!S(Q)$ is the identity on the open and zero off it by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] derives it. It is legitimate on K-flat models: $j_!Q\otimes L=j_!(Q\otimes j^*L)$ by the same stalk formula, and exact $j^*$ and $j_!$ show that $j_!Q$ stays K-flat. Define the proper $B$-linear map $S_YRq_{*,A}L\to Rq_{*,B}S_{\bar X}L$ as the transpose of $q_B^*S_YRq_{*,A}L\cong S_{\bar X}q_A^*Rq_{*,A}L\to S_{\bar X}L$. Its restriction to $A$ is the proper projection map with tensor factor $B$, followed by the inverse of the canonical restriction-of-scalars direct-image comparison [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]: transposing either map is precisely the $A$-counit tensored with $B$. The proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] is unbounded and imposes no flatness on $B$, so this map is an isomorphism. Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms because it leaves cohomology sheaves unchanged. Compose these proper and open comparisons to get $b_M$. The restriction-of-scalars comparison is only used on bounded-below $L$ and $S(L)$; the latter is bounded by Step 2. For $A\to B\to C$, transposing the twice-applied proper comparison gives the original proper counit tensored with $C$, since $(x\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes bc$. The open comparisons have exactly this formula. Hence $b_{A,C}=b_{B,C}\circ S_C(b_{A,B})$ after tensor associativity. Adjunction pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] and compactification comparisons [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] give the same map on a common refinement.

source.place: Construction of b; non-flat proper projection argument and associativity

proof.text:
First justify applying Step 3 to $G_AK$: [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] already identifies $G_AK$ with $f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}$, where $\omega_{f,A}[-2d]$ is a locally constant free rank-one sheaf. Thus it is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by the flat-model and finite-stratification calculation of Step 2, with interval shifted by $-2d$. This uses no chosen orientation. Hence $b_{G_AK}$ is defined on a bounded finite-Tor object. Define $c_K:S_XG_AK\to G_BS_YK$ by transposing $S_Y\varepsilon_A(K)\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1}$. This is natural by the adjunction bijection. For three rings, transpose $c_{B,C}(S_BK)\circ S_C(c_{A,B}(K))$. Substituting the defining counit identity twice gives $S_C\varepsilon_A(K)$ preceded by the inverse of the twice-applied $b$. Step 3 identifies this with $S_C\varepsilon_A(K)\circ b_{A,C}^{-1}$, the transpose of $c_{A,C}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the exceptional cocycle, without any faithfulness claim for restriction of scalars on derived morphisms. This definition also commutes with the smooth base-change maps of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change]: both orders, transposed, are the pulled-back original counit tensored with $B$. For the proper piece, the needed exchange/projection equality is precisely [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]; for the open piece it is the identity-on-the-open/zero-off-the-open tensor equality of Step 3. Pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] therefore proves the equality for compact supports and their transposes. Let $\phi_{A,K}:f^*K\otimes\omega_{f,A}\to G_AK$ be the canonical tensor map of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. Its transpose is $P_A(f^*K\otimes\omega_{f,A})\to K\otimes P_A\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_A(A_Y)}K$. Extending this expression to $B$ and substituting the counit identity for $c_{A_Y}$ gives exactly the transpose of $\phi_{B,S_YK}\circ(1\otimes c_{A_Y})$. The projection maps agree because their own transposes are counit tensored with identity, with the tensor associators computed in Step 2. Thus
$$c_K\circ S_X\phi_{A,K}=\phi_{B,S_YK}\circ(1\otimes c_{A_Y}).$$
The pullback and tensor identifications in this equation are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. No invertibility of $c$ has yet been assumed.

source.place: Composition (2), tensor-map part of (3), and explicit base-change mate square

proof.text: Fix the vector-bundle normalization over any Noetherian $S$. Apply [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] with $F=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and coefficient $A_n$. It gives $v_{\pi,A}:A_E(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{\pi,A}$, adjoint to the integration specified by [def-amb-vector-integration]. This orientation commutes with $A_r\to A_m$. Indeed choose the common annihilator $N=\ell^r$. The roots-of-unity lines and their reductions agree by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The projective-line splitting in [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] has components the unit and the scalar-extended Kummer Chern class of $\mathcal O(1)$. Coefficient extension carries these components to the same two components over $B$: the unit is transposed from identity; the Chern class over $A$ and over $B$ is the image of the same class over $\mathbf Z/N$. A split pair of free rank-one summands remains split under derived extension, so its inverse followed by projection onto the second summand reduces to the same trace over $B$. Restrict to $\mathbf A^1$, then iterate the ordered affine-line counits of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. The composite-counit formula $\varepsilon_{FG}=\varepsilon_F\circ F(\varepsilon_G)$ shows that each iterated trace reduces to the corresponding trace over $B$. Hence the vector-bundle traces agree on a trivializing cover. Their sources are isomorphic to $A_S[0]$ by [def-amb-vector-integration]; after extension they are $B_S[0]$. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] makes the equality a sheaf-morphism equality, so agreement on this cover proves global equality. Taking adjoints in the counit identity defining $c$ gives $c_{A_S}\circ S(v_{\pi,A})=v_{\pi,B}$, with source identified by the canonical twist comparison. This includes rank zero, where the ordered counit is the identity.

source.place: Vector-bundle factor; sk-lem-sp-reduction.proof.md, common Kummer class and two free projective-line summands

proof.text:
Put $W=X\times_YX$. The first projection $p_1$ is smooth of the same pure relative dimension $d$, by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), since it is the base change of $f$ along $f$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], $\Delta$ is a closed regular section of $p_1$ with normal bundle $T_{X/Y}$ of rank $d$. All these schemes and the deformation space are separated finite type over $k$; the Noetherian and compactification checks of Step 1 apply. The canonical base-change isomorphism [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] gives $p_2^*\omega_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_1,A}$; pulling back by $\Delta$ identifies its source with $\omega_{f,A}$. Apply [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization] to $(p_1,\Delta)$ and compose its $\delta$ with $z^*v_{\pi,A}^{-1}$ from Step 5. This is the orientation $\alpha_{f,A}$ in the statement, and every factor is an isomorphism. To check its coefficient compatibility, use the same deformation space for $A=A_r$ and $B=A_m$. Write $F_A$ for its family object and $C_A$ for its $t=1$ fibre. The maps $c$ of Step 4 give $e_F:S(F_A)\to F_B$ and $e_C:S(C_A)\to C_B$, with these fibre restrictions, by the base-change equality proved there. The two maps
$$\kappa_B\circ e_F,\qquad a^*e_C\circ S(\kappa_A):S(F_A)\longrightarrow a^*C_B$$
agree at $t=1$, both being $e_C$. Neither $e_F$ nor $e_C$ is assumed invertible at this stage. They agree everywhere: by the new lemma and the rank-one flatness, remove $[2d]$ and identify their source and target with pullbacks of rank-one locally constant sheaves on $X$. Their sheaf of homomorphisms is itself pulled back from $X$, so this uniqueness argument applies to arbitrary morphisms between these lines, not only to isomorphisms. Locally trivialize those two sheaves. A difference is then a section of the constant coefficient sheaf $B$ over $\mathbf A^1$, whose zero locus is open and closed on each geometric fibre and contains $t=1$. Every such affine-line fibre is connected, so the difference vanishes. These are actual degree-zero sheaf maps by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. Restrict the resulting equality at $t=0$ and invert the two $\kappa$'s to obtain
$$\delta_B\circ e_C=e_0\circ S(\delta_A).$$
Combining with the base-change compatibility in Step 4 and the vector-bundle compatibility in Step 5 proves
$$\alpha_{f,B}\circ c_{A_Y}=S(\alpha_{f,A})$$
under the canonical twist identifications. This checks equality of morphisms using rank-one sheaves, not equality of arbitrary derived morphisms on stalks.

source.place: Three diagonal factors; sk-lem-sp-reduction-compatibilities.proof.md (3), normalized family comparison at t=1 and t=0

proof.text: Define the ordinary $\gamma_{A,K_0}$ by the three factors displayed in the statement. The orientation is an isomorphism by Step 6 and the tensor map is an isomorphism by [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]; hence their composite is an isomorphism, natural in $K_0$. The twist line is locally free rank one by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The bounded flat model in Step 2, pulled back using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and tensored with that line, gives the Tor interval $[a-2d,b-2d]$. Exact pullback takes the finite stratification of each cohomology sheaf to its inverse-image stratification on $X$, and on each stratum it preserves finite locally constant sheaves. Tensoring a locally free rank-one line preserves this property. Thus $f^*K_0(d)[2d]$, and therefore $G_AK_0$, is bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude. For $d=0$, $f$ is separated etale of finite type between Noetherian schemes. By [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] its compact support is identified with etale sum extension $f_{\Sigma!}$, the compact-support adjunction with $f_{\Sigma!}\dashv f^*$ including the sum/evaluation counit, and the compact-support base-change exchange with the sum-extension exchange; [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] gives the resulting identification $f^*\cong f^\times$, so $\omega_{f,A}\cong A_X$. Under these identifications each factor of $\alpha_{f,A}$ is the identity. First, the base-change map of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] for $p_1$ is the transpose of the pulled-back counit through the compact-support exchange; by the normalization lemma this is the transpose of the pulled-back sum counit through the sum exchange, and on geometric stalks both are the sum over the same fibre points, so it is the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism $p_2^*f^*\cong p_1^*f^*$. Second, $\Delta$ is open and closed in $W$ (unramified and separated), so on the deformation the component through the section is $\mathbf A^1_X$ mapping isomorphically to $\mathbf A^1_X$, with $\widetilde s$ an open and closed section of the etale $\widetilde g$; by the same two identifications $F\cong A_{\mathbf A^1_X}$ and $C\cong A_X$, the fibre identifications are the canonical pullback ones, and the identity map is normalized at $t=1$, so by uniqueness it is $\kappa$ and $\delta$ is the identity. Third, at rank zero $\pi=1_X$ and the vector integration is the identity trace [def-amb-vector-integration]. Finally the transpose of the tensor map at $\omega\cong A_X$ is $f_{\Sigma!}f^*K\cong K\otimes f_{\Sigma!}A_X\to K$, the sum counit tensored with $K$; on geometric stalks this is the sum map $\bigoplus K_{\bar y}\to K_{\bar y}$, which is the sum counit at $K$. Hence $\gamma$ at $d=0$ is the inverse-image identification $f^*K\cong f^\times K$ of the etale sum adjunction, with its given counit.

source.place: Three-factor purity map and its constructible finite-Tor restriction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $C_Xf^*\cong Lf^*C_Y$. The open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] and the proper comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] compose to $C_YP_A\cong Rf_{!,A}C_X$. The latter proper map is the adjoint-of-counit map explicitly specified in its statement, so these comparisons transport the Hom adjunction and its actual counit. On the right, by the definition in this item $Rf_A^!K=C_XG_AK_0$; Step 7 proves that this object lies in the stated subcategory. Full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and the origin equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] identify different choices of $K_0$ and make the transported $\gamma$ natural. Since $C$ preserves tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], it carries all finite coefficient comparisons and their defining counit identities to those in the statement. For the proper part this follows by transposing the same counit square, and for the open part by the identity/zero formula. The comparisons apply to bounded-below objects: all inputs have the bounds of Steps 2 and 7, and proper direct image is left t-exact. The source of the compact-support coefficient comparison, if computed by an unbounded resolution of $B$ over $A$, is identified by Step 3 with $P_BS_XM$, a bounded-below object, before the site comparison is applied.

source.place: Transport through the fully faithful finite constructible comparisons, including counit

proof.text:
The pullback/twist comparison $\lambda$ is the tensor/pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the canonical finite twist comparison of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Combine the tensor-map identity of Step 4 with $\alpha_Bc_{A_Y}=S\alpha_A$ from Step 6. Substituting the three-factor formula for $\gamma$ and cancelling $\alpha_B$ gives
$$c_K\circ S_X\gamma_{A,K}=\gamma_{B,S_YK}\circ\lambda_K.$$
Both $S_X\gamma_A$ and $\gamma_B\lambda$ are isomorphisms, so this proves $c_K$ is an isomorphism. It also proves that the adjoint traces reduce, by the defining counit identity of $c$; no separately normalized trace is assumed. The cocycle for $b$ is Step 3, the cocycle for $c$ is Step 4, and those for pullback and twist are the tensor reassociation $(q\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto q\otimes bc$ and the composition of the root power maps. Thus the purity square has the same two-stage and direct versions for $A_r\to A_m\to A_n$, including equal levels. At $K=A_{n,Y}$ the source is the locally free line $A_{n,X}(d)[2d]$, so its only cohomology is in degree $-2d$; the isomorphism gives the same for the target. Its derived reductions are the corresponding free lines, with the cocycle just proved.
